BiblicalUsage: Hezekiah uses this word for the slow, careful walk of a man who has faced death and been spared, going softly through the rest of his years in bitterness of soul. The psalmist uses it the same way, remembering how he once went with the multitude up to the house of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word pictures repentance as a pace, not a moment: a life that has been humbled walks differently from then on.
